- [USER_SAID] Responsibilities of the Instructional Designer include:
  - Working closely with faculty or business subject matter experts to design, create, and deliver online, blended, and instructor-led classroom training courses and documentation.
  - Developing content for learning or knowledge management systems.
  - Conducting learning and business needs analysis.
  - Drafting expected learning outcomes that align with course goals.
  - Determining scope and sequence of content, identifying impacted or target audiences, and relevant pre-requisites for learner success.
  - Designing/implementing course evaluation plans.
  - Devising modes of assessment to measure the effectiveness of the course.
  - Writing effective copy, instructional materials, and audio/video scripts.
  - Producing learning materials in various formats including print, graphics, audio, video, and multimedia.
  - Using e-learning authoring tools to upload instructional content to websites, e-learning platforms, or learning management systems.
  - May develop and deliver train-the-trainer programs and deliver in-person instruction of complex information to participants.
  - Providing training on instructional technologies and tools.

  - Master’s degree, formal training, or certification in Instructional Design is preferable.
